issues.claim: Law 1 (1) makes a deck passing over a wall no crossing of the gate law (base l. 2700-2702) and law 1 (3) lays a ring dated after a road deck beneath it ungated (l. 2714-2718; row (d) l. 2914; T110-2 (3)'s c14 fixture, l. 19308-19314: 'the arterial on the deck pinning no gate and S5b's count read on ground part 0'). §4.8 Gates (l. 8369, 'so counted') and §5.3's gate row (l. 9938, 'on ground part 0; a deck passing over a trace is no crossing') count so; two readers do not. V12's geo metric `wall.ungated` (V12 l. 1167: 'arterial ways crossing a curtain at no gate'), computed alike on the references' 2-D captures and our MeasureInput whose ways carry `part` (l. 350, 1406), and whose reading rules (l. 1124-1129) exclude only `retaining`, counts the S4 arterial's deck over a stage-2 curtain; base §13.5's P row 'towers and gates' (l. 20059: 'ungated crossings 0 ... roads leaving each walled stage = its N main gates, plus a harbour gate') has no part-0 qualifier and no carried way's gate. On a parity seed whose viaduct passes over a later ring a correct build fails the P bar under the literal reading and passes under law 1 (1): two builders, two values, a named check failing a correct build. One fix with scope (§13.5).

V12 l. 1167, the `wall.ungated` cell: "arterial ways crossing a curtain at no gate" -> "arterial ways on ground part 0 crossing a curtain at no gate (a way's `part` >= 1 never counted: a deck passing over a curtain is no crossing, §2.7's laws, law 1 (1), (3); §5.3's gate row)". 2. V12 l. 1128, after "`wall.*`, `gate.count` and `wall.ungated` read `wall` features only, never `retaining`" add "; `wall.ungated` reads ways of `part` 0 only (§2.7's laws, law 1 (1))". 3. END for scope, base §13.5's "towers and gates" row (l. 20059): "ungated crossings 0" -> "ungated crossings 0 (on ground part 0; a deck passing over a trace is no crossing, §2.7's laws, law 1 (1))"; and "roads leaving each walled stage = its N main gates, plus a harbour gate of §4.2 S3 (7) where one was placed" -> "roads leaving each walled stage on ground part 0 = its gate count by §5.3's gate row (its N main gates, a harbour gate of §4.2 S3 (7) where one was placed, and any gate a carried way standing before the stage takes, §2.7's laws, law 2 *Carried way*)".

issues.claim: Law 1 (8) (base l. 2729-2733): from the commit that lays a raised way's arch vaults 'a span read `vault` has its chamber' with no exception. V04 §3.5.4 (d) (1), the one rule that lays it, makes none on a degenerate span: 'An inset rectangle below `minEdge` on a side is no chamber: the span stays unvaulted in the model and is reported' (V04 l. 1707-1708; U-SYS edge row l. 2389). Reachable: the support step (3) slides a station with only an upper bound on its neighbouring spans (base l. 2547-2549) and (4) widens each pier to max(0.2 x span, 1.5 m) (l. 2559-2560), so two stations slid together leave a span whose 60 cm-inset rectangle (V04 l. 623) falls under `minEdgeCm` 25 (base l. 602); the span rule never reads that width (l. 3376-3393) and nothing lies across, so law 1 (8) reads it `vault`. The readers already split: V09's badge counts 'the arch vaults V04 §3.5.4 (d) lays' (V09 l. 3060-3062), V10 names 'its arch vault where V04 §3.5.4 (d) lays one' (V10 l. 1686), CityJSON's `BridgeRoom` follows the chamber (l. 16703), while glTF closes the span by end walls (l. 16702) and GeoJSON exports `vault` (l. 16698), against T-ER-12's 'one reading' (l. 15463). A correct V04 build breaks law 1 (8) and fails T-V4-62 ('an arch vault in exactly each `vault` span §2.7's laws read `vault`', V04 l. 3163) and T110-4's 'law 1 after every commit' (l. 2887) wherever a degenerate span arises. One fix with V04 and rendering.

END for rendering, §8.11's T-ER-12 outcome cell (l. 15463): "a span's `use` one reading in GeoJSON's `span` feature, glTF's end walls and CityJSON's `BridgeRoom`" -> "a span's `use` one reading in GeoJSON's `span` feature and glTF's end walls, and CityJSON's `BridgeRoom` wherever V04 lays its arch vault (law 1 (8))".

issues.claim: §4.5's daylight casters (base l. 6873) restate law 1 (7) and narrow it: 'walls (a run beneath a road deck's standing span capped at the lowest soffit there, an aqueduct capping none: §2.7's laws, law 1 (7))'. Law 1 (7) caps the band beneath a standing span 'or a standing support bearing one' (l. 2726-2728) and *the cap* caps a run across a support at the lowest soffit of the spans it bears (l. 3087-3091; T110-2 (3) l. 19311). The citation governs, so the top is one, but the model's shade, §8.4 (l. 14386-14387, 14611-14612) and §11.1 must read one top, and only the latter are under T-ER-12. Part H's head: a clause restating a law is written as its citation.

issues.claim: §5.4's `reshaped` entry (base l. 9991) names its `entity` 'a locked, pinned or declared wall, raised way or arch vault whose shape a meeting changed'. Law 4's (G2) shows only a change to a thing held in placement — 'a placement-locked structure, part or way' (l. 2865-2869) — and *held* says a thing declared or placed by hand holds nothing unless locked (l. 2656-2657; Part L's correction 6); the entry's own `ReshapeChange` has `wayRerouted`, a held ground way's course (l. 9992; law 2 (b) l. 2818-2819), whose entity the list omits. V09's `report.moved.reshaped` line (V09 l. 2093) and the history's report-entry lines show what the entry holds. Law 4 governs; the comment is the slip.

(b) Citations by the tables' names: l. 978 '§2.7's crossing table', l. 2468 '(§2.7's crossing table, *beneath*)', l. 2481 'by §2.7's crossing table'. (c) V01 §1.2's hook row (l. 201) lists `raisedWays.structure` (`clearanceCm`, `clearWidthM`, `squareDeg`) though §3.17.3 (2) reads `stripMarginM` (l. 2464; V01's constants line l. 2139). Nothing built changes.

At a meeting §2.7 keeps what an unlocked chamber seats: 'A building seated there and not locked holds nothing: its chamber is removed under a wall laid later as any chamber is, the building kept in existence as its kind's are' (base l. 3133-3135; *held* l. 2656-2657, 'it keeps its existence'; veto item 10). issues.claim: E-V12-1's register line (V12 l. 2177) says `stripMarginM` is 'read by §4.6 S8 and by §2.7's laws — the strip, the ends, the zone and a held building's strip of their terms —'. A held building's strip is a span's strip — 'the deck's plan between its two piers' inner faces without that margin' (base l. 2614-2616) — widened by the wall strips' width (l. 2640-2641); it reads no margin. A register line naming a reader the cell does not have; nothing built changes.

held_notes.note: A span selected in the hit stack carries the path `spans/<n>`, while §7.1's binding, V09 §4.20.6 (2) and V10's `span` row key a span `spans/<a>-<b>` by its bounding piers' keys (E-D15).

'On a viaduct over a street with a walled-up span: ... the deck, the span, the arch vault and the street' — a street's corridor across a span keeps it `open` (law 1 (8)), so the fixture needs the street under a neighbouring span within the hit radius; it does not say so.
